prompt:
Image 1 is a flat lay of a Pickleball kit, photographed from the front.

Photograph THAT SAME KIT from the BACK — the same garments, turned over:
- the shirt, laid flat and face DOWN, so its back is what you see
- the shorts below it, also turned so their back is what you see
EXACTLY ONE of each. No socks, no shoes, no ball, nothing else in the frame.

Everything carries over from image 1 unchanged: the same colours, the same fabric, the
same cut, the same collar, and above all the SAME PANELS AND
TRIM — a stripe, a panel or a piping that exists on the front continues around to the
back exactly as the garment's construction would carry it. Nothing is added that image 1
does not have, and nothing that image 1 has quietly disappears.

SLEEVES: this is the same garment as image 1, so it has exactly the same sleeves. If the
shirt in image 1 has short sleeves, this one has short sleeves and is NOT a sleeveless
vest or a tank top. If image 1 is sleeveless, this one is sleeveless. Look at image 1 and
copy what is there.

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: A COPPER short-sleeved athletic T-SHIRT exactly as photo2.png shows it: a plain round neck and short set-in sleeves, with a LIGHTER COPPER contrast SEAM piped along each shoulder, running from the neckline out to the underarm — that lighter shoulder seam is the only trim on it, and the rest of the shirt is plain copper. It fits close but is not tight. The club badge sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about a palm across: the copperline-kingfishers mark exactly as the crest artwork draws it — an upright rounded PATCH with its top two corners clipped, in pale cream, carrying the kingfisher diving head-first straight down with its wings swept back into a dart and its dagger beak at the bottom, in copper. It is the ONLY mark on the shirt. NO maker's logo, NO club name, NO player name, NO number and no lettering of any kind. The BACK of the shirt is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it stays PLAIN COPPER: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere on it. Pickleball does not number a shirt, and a number across her back would be a mark this shirt does not have.
- shorts: PLAIN COPPER athletic SHORTS exactly as photo2.png and photo3.png show them: the same copper as the shirt, cut short to mid-thigh with a plain flat elasticated waistband, a soft loose leg and no stripe, no piping and no side panel. NO maker's logo, no number and no lettering on them. photo3.png shows her training on an outdoor court in a copper sleeveless TANK with the same shorts; the tank is training wear, and the DECISION for every pose is the SHORT-SLEEVED t-shirt from photo2.png, which is her match kit.
- socks: PLAIN WHITE ANKLE SOCKS, sitting just above the shoe collar with a short band of white showing between the shoe and the bare ankle, exactly as photo3.png shows them. No stripe, no colour band and no maker's mark. The same pair in every frame.
- footwear: ENTIRELY WHITE COURT SHOES — white upper, white laces and white sole, with NO grey panels and no contrast colour anywhere on them, exactly as photo3.png shows them — a flat non-marking court sole and a slightly cushioned midsole, as photo3.png shows them. Completely PLAIN and UNBRANDED — no stripes device, no swoosh, no maker's mark and no lettering on the upper or the sole. The same pair in every frame, clean.
- equipment: A PICKLEBALL PADDLE and a BALL, both plain. The paddle has a flat rigid SOLID FACE — no strings, no open throat, no oval head — in light beige, with a BLACK edge guard around it and a BLACK wrapped handle. The face is COMPLETELY BLANK: no graphic, no swirl, no logo, no model name and no lettering on either side of it. NO BALL appears in any photograph; the DECISION is that where a pose needs one it is a plain YELLOW perforated plastic pickleball with round holes, unbranded, and it appears nowhere else. In photo2.png there is also a plain towel and a plain unlabelled water bottle on the bench beside her; the DECISION for the poses is that she carries the PADDLE and, where the action needs it, the BALL — and nothing else: no bag, no bottle, no towel.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it — a real team badge, not a printed graphic across the front. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

THE BACK OF THE SHIRT CARRIES NO NUMBER. This sport does not number the back of the shirt, so the back is plain: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere else on it, unless the kit description above explicitly gives it one. Add no mark the description does not name.
NEVER any lettering: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no word of any kind.
Nothing sits inside, on top of or overlapping the numerals — a badge, if the description
calls for one, is small, clear of the number, and the right way round.

Hard requirements:
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no wear, no sweat marks.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- The same plain light grey surface and the same even lighting as image 1.
- No text of any kind beyond the number, no labels, no neck tag, no watermark.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
